characterList.name: Bob

content_metadata.description: Bob gives an overview of the pros and cons of using trekking poles while hiking.

qAndA.answer: Bob shows the Leki Cristallo trekking poles.
qAndA.question: What type of trekking poles does Bob show?

qAndA.answer: Besides adjusting the height for a more comfortable hike, Bob likes that he can adjust them to set up his trekking pole tent.
qAndA.question: What's the main benefit Bob finds in using adjustable trekking poles?

qAndA.answer: Bob says trekking poles help him hike further by helping him maintain a steady pace and posture, saving energy on his legs and breathing better.
qAndA.question: According to Bob, besides providing stability, how do trekking poles benefit his hiking experience?

qAndA.answer: While acknowledging that's a valid option, Bob prefers buying trekking poles as they have adjustable height, which provides more flexibility and a custom feel to his hiking experience.
qAndA.question: Why does Bob prefer buying trekking poles over using sticks found in the woods?

qAndA.answer: No. Bob lays out pros and cons for the viewer to decide what's best for them. He also hints that he prefers trekking poles.

narrativeProgression.description: Bob starts talking about the pros and cons of using trekking poles.
Bob shows the trekking poles he uses and explains how they can be adjusted to different heights.
Bob explains how trekking poles provide added balance.
Bob says trekking poles can help maintain a steadier pace on the trail, especially going uphill.
Bob mentions that trekking poles help him keep an upright posture.
Bob says the main con of using trekking poles is that it's an extra item to carry, which adds weight to his backpack.
Bob explains that trekking poles can experience wear and tear with use, as they have moving parts that can break.
Bob says trekking poles can get expensive, so it's just another expense to incorporate.
